contact_edits.before: There's a well-staged fight, but for the most part Leslie O'Dell's production can make the play nothing but dull. Christopher Stanton, once past his early contortions, gives a decent account of Will, but Mark McGrinder's Sam is done in by a continuous vocal smirk, which is intended to convey ambiguous cheerfulness; his attempts at bolstering his companion's morale sound positively nannyish. Perhaps, if a playwright wants to get us thinking about modern warfare, he should choose a different conflict. It's true that 1914-18 was the entrance to the chamber of horrors in which we still live, but dramatically and otherwise it's been done -- to use a rather too appropriate phrase -- to death. There have been innumerable literary and dramatic treatments of this war, and it's hard to add anything new. At any rate, it hasn't happened here. It's cruel, but true, that the best comment on this play is its title. - Performances run through Nov. 10. For tickets, call 416-866-8666.
